title: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 06 (Board Paper Standard I (Full Book))
subject: english-12

questions.question: In 'Using the Scientific Method', how did our ancestors view natural disasters like famines and plagues?

options.A: As biological imbalances to be corrected by vaccination
options.B: As punishments from angry deities or evil spirits that must be appeased through magical charms

questions.explanation: Primitive people attributed disease and crop failure to evil spirits and witchcraft because they lacked scientific knowledge of germs and meteorology.

questions.question: In 1800, what was the typical life expectancy of a newborn child in European towns compared to modern times?

options.A: Around 70 years due to unpolluted nature
options.B: Less than 35 years due to severe infant mortality and rampant epidemics

questions.explanation: Over half of children died before the age of six, and average life expectancy was under 35 years prior to modern medicine and sanitation.

questions.question: In 'End of Term', what does the phrase 'the maid's grim knock' signify?

options.A: The delivery of urgent telegrams
options.B: The daily rude awakening that terminated peaceful slumber and commenced the school day

questions.explanation: The maid knocking on the bedroom door was the dreaded signal that sleep was over and the harsh routine of school had begun.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the word 'hypochondriac':

options.A: A person suffering from chronic heart failure
options.B: A person who is abnormally anxious about their health and imagines illnesses they do not have
options.C: A physician specializing in bone surgery

questions.explanation: A hypochondriac suffers from irrational health anxiety and incessantly diagnoses nonexistent medical conditions in themselves.

questions.question: According to McKenzie, if global population continues to expand unchecked, the world will inevitably face:

options.A: Catastrophic resource depletion, water scarcity, environmental collapse, and widespread conflict
options.B: Universal peace and brotherhood
options.C: A sudden reduction in carbon emissions
options.D: An expansion of agricultural land into the oceans

questions.explanation: Uncontrolled exponential population growth threatens arable land, fresh water supplies, and geopolitical stability.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to face the music'?

options.A: To listen to an orchestral symphony
options.B: To confront unpleasant consequences or criticism for one's actions with courage
options.D: To play an instrument in public

questions.explanation: 'Facing the music' means bravely confronting the repercussions or penalties of one's blunders.

questions.question: What was Churchill's position on the traditional roll-call at Harrow?

options.A: He was called first because his name was Winston.
options.B: He was summoned almost last because boys were called alphabetically, and his name began with 'S' (Spencer-Churchill), placing him at the bottom of the list.

questions.explanation: Spencer-Churchill put him near the very end of the roll-call, making his bottom academic rank visible to the entire school.

questions.question: What is 'fesh-fesh' in Saharan geography as experienced by Christopher?

options.A: Deep underground freshwater springs
options.B: A fine, treacherous dust that looks solid but collapses under weight like quicksand
options.C: A type of date palm fruit
options.D: A hot green tea served by Tuaregs

questions.explanation: 'Fesh-fesh' is powdered desert dust beneath a deceptive crust that easily traps heavy vehicles.

questions.question: What was the popular moniker given to Penicillin after its miracle efficacy was demonstrated in treating WW2 battle casualties?

options.A: 'The Wonder Drug'
options.B: 'The Black Salve'

questions.explanation: Penicillin saved countless Allied soldiers from septic gangrene and pneumonia, earning universal fame as 'The Wonder Drug'.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'Fleming was modest and objected _____ being lionized by the global press.'

options.A: at
options.B: to

questions.explanation: The verb 'object' requires the preposition 'to' followed by a gerund ('objected to being lionized').

questions.question: What was the significance of the Battle of Sakarya (1921)?

options.A: It was the military turning point where Kemal halted the Greek advance on Ankara after 22 days of desperate combat.
options.B: It was a minor border skirmish with no historical effect.
options.C: It resulted in the surrender of Ankara.
options.D: It was a naval battle in the Mediterranean.

questions.explanation: Sakarya broke the Greek military offensive and earned Mustafa Kemal the rank of Marshal and the title 'Gazi'.

questions.question: What was the historical impact of the Treaty of Sèvres (1920)?

options.A: It was the Allied blueprint that attempted to dismember Turkey, which Kemal and the Nationalists furiously repudiated and defeated in battle.
options.B: It granted Turkey control of Egypt.
options.C: It was signed by Atatürk in Ankara.
options.D: It brought universal democracy to Europe.

questions.explanation: The puppet Ottoman government signed Sèvres, but Kemal's National Assembly rejected it as a death warrant and destroyed it through armed victory.

questions.question: What was the reaction of Brookfield masters when Chips announced his engagement to Katherine Bridges?

options.A: Shock and envy that such an ordinary middle-aged master had won the hand of such a dazzling, charming, and vivacious young woman
options.B: Total indifference
options.C: They expelled Chips from the common room

questions.explanation: The bachelor masters and school wives were astonished that quiet old Chipping had captured the heart of such a brilliant young lady.

questions.question: What was Chips' standard joke regarding the Latin word 'lex' and Roman law?

options.A: He made punning quips connecting Latin grammar rules to the pranks of contemporary schoolboys.
options.B: He said Latin was useless.
options.D: He made boys translate statutes backward.

questions.explanation: Chips developed a repertoire of harmless, gentle classical jokes that elicited loyal laughter in the classroom year after year.

questions.question: What is the synonym of the word 'obstinate' as used to describe Chips' resistance to Ralston?

options.A: Yielding and submissive
options.B: Stubbornly adhering to one's purpose or opinion; unyielding

questions.explanation: 'Obstinate' means stubborn, inflexible, or steadfastly refusing to budge.

questions.question: Identify the part of speech of 'warmly' in: 'Sir John Rivers greeted Chips warmly.'

options.A: Adverb of manner
options.B: Abstract noun

questions.explanation: 'Warmly' modifies the action verb 'greeted', describing how the action was performed (adverb of manner).

questions.question: What was Chatteris' cause of death during the war?

options.A: Diabetes and physical overwork at the age of forty-one
options.B: Killed by a bomb in London

questions.explanation: Chatteris worked himself to death trying to keep Brookfield running while suffering from severe diabetes.

questions.question: Identify the grammatical role of 'Good-bye' in the title 'Good-bye, Mr. Chips':

options.A: Interjection used as a valediction/farewell
options.B: Transitive verb

questions.explanation: 'Good-bye' is an interjection expressing farewell, derived from the archaic phrase 'God be with ye'.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'once in a blue moon'?

options.A: Every full moon night
options.B: Extremely rarely or almost never

questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' is an established idiom for an event that occurs very infrequently.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The headmaster concurred _____ the decision of the governors.'

options.A: with
options.B: at

questions.explanation: One concurs 'with' a person or decision, meaning to agree or share an opinion.
